title: The Overgrowth Remembers the Clearing

features.name: half-remembered homestead
features.desc-on-touch: A small house pixel-rendered in tan and rust, half-choked with grass. You remember standing in its doorway before the green learned to climb.

features.name: the clearing's doorway
features.desc-on-touch: An arch of green learning where the open paddock used to begin. The boundary has become kind.

features.name: diagnostic posts
features.desc-on-touch: The render's assertion: wireframe marker posts at the cardinal points where the clearing once was measured. They are being overgrown slowly.

features.name: growth-line fence
features.desc-on-touch: A rusted fence that has learned to carry vines instead of hold them back. The metal sings faintly in the wind.

features.name: the memory-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A shallow depression collecting rain and reflection. The water shows you the clearing as it was, then as it grows.

features.name: the render's margin
features.desc-on-touch: Where the diagnostic terminal's tan ink meets the overgrowth's green. The two are learning to share the page.

inscription: what grows in an empty place knows it will be forgotten again

reverie.title: REVERIE — standing in the clearing before it forgot itself
narr: You stand in the middle of bare earth—no grass yet, just
the possibility. She's looking at the horizon line where the
tree-stand begins. "This place doesn't know it's empty," she
says. "It thinks it's waiting." A single leaf spirals down between
you. By next season it will be indistinguishable from the rest.
She's already gone—you know that standing here. Gone and not.

exits.label: back up through the clearing toward diagnostic inference
where the grid learns to bend into orchards
into deeper growth where the archive grows its own roots
where fences teach vegetables their secret names
